what: Emitting the per-party check in the circuit, predicted before the generator was changed
the_change: secret_input() currently reads one share from each party and returns the sum, so the shares are gone by the time the check runs. The per-party version folds each share into its own party's accumulator AS IT IS READ --- the coefficient is a compile-time constant, so public times secret stays local and costs no communication --- and then opens one accumulator per party. The masks stop being split across nodes and become one value read from each node.

predictions.predicted: unchanged against the aggregate check, and +1 against no check at all
predictions.why: the n openings do not depend on each other, so MP-SPDZ batches them into one round
predictions.falsifiable: any increase over the aggregate check's round count

predictions.predicted: about 3 kB more than the aggregate check at a wide field, which is +0.02 percent
predictions.arithmetic: the aggregate check at 40-bit coefficients opens 1 value; per-party opens 7. One opening costs about 4 field elements per party (the multiplication measurement puts two openings at 8.0), so 6 extra openings are 24 elements per party, 384 bytes, 2.7 kB across seven --- against 19.37 MB for the quote.
predictions.note: an earlier estimate said 'under half a percent'. That was pessimistic by more than an order of magnitude, because it costed an opening as though it were a multiplication.

predictions.predicted: free. Public coefficient times secret share is local arithmetic; only the opening travels.
unchanged --- every arm is verified against the cleartext reference, and the check adds openings without touching the computation

the_workflow_this_completes: maker deals and publishes commitments -> node checks its own share -> circuit folds each share into its party's accumulator -> circuit opens n values -> anyone recomputes the coefficients from the published commitments and checks each opening -> a failing one names a node.
